claim: The cerebral cortex contains multiple areas with distinctive cytoarchitectonic patterns.
source: The cerebral cortex contains multiple areas with distinctive cytoarchitectonic patterns, but the cellular mechanisms underlying the emergence of this diversity remain unclear.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that establishes the context of the study.

claim: Progenitor cells generate pyramidal cell lineages with a wide range of sizes and laminar configurations.
source: Our experimental results indicate that progenitor cells generate pyramidal cell lineages with a wide range of sizes and laminar configurations.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental results presented in the manuscript.

claim: The outcomes of progenitor cell neurogenesis are compatible with a stochastic model in which progenitor cells undergo probabilistic decisions.
source: Mathematical modeling indicates that these outcomes are compatible with a stochastic model of cortical neurogenesis in which progenitor cells undergo a series of probabilistic decisions that lead to the specification of very heterogeneous progenies.
evidence: This claim is supported by mathematical modeling results presented in the manuscript.

claim: The stochastic mechanism of cortical neurogenesis is capable of generating diverse cytoarchitectures that characterize distinct neocortical areas.
source: Our findings support a mechanism for cortical neurogenesis whose flexibility would make it capable to generate the diverse cytoarchitectures that characterize distinct neocortical areas.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental and modeling results.

claim: Pyramidal cells are the most abundant class of neurons in the cerebral cortex.
source: The most abundant class of neurons in the cerebral cortex are excitatory projection neurons, also known as pyramidal cells (PCs).
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge.

claim: Pyramidal cells in the neocortex can be classified into several subclasses with unique laminar distributions, projection patterns and electrophysiological properties.
source: In the neocortex, PCs can be further classified into several subclasses with unique laminar distributions, projection patterns and electrophysiological properties (Greig et al., 2013; Jabaudon, 2017; Lodato and Arlotta, 2015)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Several dozen distinct transcriptional signatures can be distinguished among pyramidal cells.
source: currently available data suggest that several dozen distinct transcriptional signatures can be distinguished among them (Tasic et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The relative abundance of different types of pyramidal cells largely determines the distinct cytoarchitectonical patterns observed across different regions of the mammalian neocortex.
source: The relative abundance of the different types of PCs largely determines the distinct cytoarchitectonical patterns observed across different regions of the mammalian neocortex (Brodmann and Gary, 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The diversity of excitatory neurons emerges from radial glial cells (RGCs) in the ventricular zone of the developing neocortex.
source: The diversity of excitatory neurons emerges from progenitor cells in the ventricular zone (VZ) of the developing neocortex known as radial glial cells (RGCs) (Malatesta et al., 2000; Miyata et al., 2001; Noctor et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: RGCs divide symmetrically to expand the progenitor pool during early stages of corticogenesis.
source: RGCs divide symmetrically to expand the progenitor pool during early stages of corticogenesis.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about RGC behavior.

claim: RGCs undergo asymmetric cell divisions to generate clones of pyramidal cells directly or indirectly via intermediate progenitor cells.
source: Subsequently, they undergo asymmetric cell divisions to generate clones of PCs directly or indirectly via intermediate progenitor cells (IPCs) (Lui et al., 2011; Taverna et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The radial unit hypothesis postulates that pyramidal cells in a given radial column are clonally related.
source: The characteristic vertical organization of migrating PCs in the developing neocortex led to the 'radial unit hypothesis', which postulates that PCs in a given radial column are clonally related (Rakic, 1988).
evidence: This claim describes a hypothesis from previous literature.

claim: RGCs are multipotent and generate all types of excitatory neurons following an inside-out temporal sequence.
source: The most commonly accepted view of cortical neurogenesis is based on the notion that RGCs are multipotent and generate all types of excitatory neurons following an exquisite inside-out temporal sequence (Leone et al., 2008; Molyneaux et al., 2007; Rakic et al., 1994).
evidence: This claim describes a commonly accepted view supported by citations.

claim: Progenitor cells cultured in vitro reproduce the temporal sequence of cortical neurogenesis.
source: Consistently, progenitor cells cultured in vitro reproduce the temporal sequence of cortical neurogenesis (Gaspard et al., 2008; Shen et al., 2006)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous experimental work.

claim: Cortical progenitors identified by the expression of Fezf2 and Sox9 are multipotent in vivo.
source: genetic fate mapping experiments have shown that cortical progenitors identified by the expression of the transcription factors Fezf2 and Sox9 are multipotent in vivo (Guo et al., 2013; Kaplan et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous genetic fate mapping experiments.

claim: Some studies have suggested the existence of fate-restricted cortical progenitors that only generate pyramidal cells for certain layers of the neocortex.
source: In contrast to this view, other studies have suggested the existence of fate-restricted cortical progenitors, which would only generate PCs for certain layers of the neocortex (Franco et al., 2012; García-Moreno and Molnár, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Recent clonal analyses led to the conclusion that progenitor cell behavior conforms to a deterministic program through which individual RGCs consistently generate the same neuronal output.
source: Consistent with this view, recent clonal analyses of the developing neocortex led to the conclusion that progenitor cell behavior conforms to a deterministic program through which individual RGCs consistently generate the same neuronal output (Gao et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous clonal analysis study.

claim: Retroviral infection leads to the labeling of only one of the two daughter cells resulting from the division of the infected progenitor cell.
source: Since a single copy of the viral vector is stably integrated into the host genome, retroviral infection leads to the labeling of only one of the two daughter cells resulting from the division of the infected progenitor cell.
evidence: This is a statement about the mechanism of retroviral labeling based on established knowledge.

claim: The onset of cortical neurogenesis begins immediately before E12.5.
source: Consistent with previous reports using other methods (Gao et al., 2014), these results indicated that the onset of cortical neurogenesis begins immediately before E12.5
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and consistent with previous reports.

claim: At E12.5, most VZ progenitor cells are already neurogenic.
source: these results indicated that the onset of cortical neurogenesis begins immediately before E12.5, and that at this stage most VZ progenitor cells are already neurogenic.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from retroviral labeling experiments.

claim: Most VZ progenitor cells (63%) infected with retroviruses at E12.5 produce translaminar lineages containing neurons in both deep and superficial layers of the neocortex.
source: Consistent with classical models of cortical neurogenesis, we found that most VZ progenitor cells (63%) infected with retroviruses at E12.5 produce translaminar lineages containing neurons in both deep (V and VI) and superficial (II-III and IV) layers of the neocortex (Figure 2b,e).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: 15% of lineages labeled at E12.5 are confined to deep layers of the neocortex.
source: However, we also observed a substantial fraction of lineages in which PCs were confined to either deep (Figure 2c,e) or superficial (Figure 2d,e) layers (15% and 22%, respectively).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: 22% of lineages labeled at E12.5 are confined to superficial layers of the neocortex.
source: However, we also observed a substantial fraction of lineages in which PCs were confined to either deep (Figure 2c,e) or superficial (Figure 2d,e) layers (15% and 22%, respectively).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: IPCs exclusively generate one-cell and two-cell clones at E12.5.
source: We analyzed 73 IPC-derived lineages at P21 and exclusively found one-cell and two-cell clones, with no evidence for larger clones within our sample (Figure 2—figure supplement 1b–d).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from Tbr2CreERT2 lineage tracing.

claim: The vast majority of MADM lineages adopt a translaminar configuration.
source: Consistent with the retroviral lineage tracing experiments, we found that the vast majority of MADM lineages adopt a translaminar configuration (Figure 3b,d).
evidence: This claim is supported by MADM experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Approximately 7% of MADM lineages are restricted to deep layers of the neocortex.
source: In addition, we also identified some lineages in which PCs were confined to layers V and VI, thereby confirming the existence of cortical lineages restricted to deep layers of the neocortex (Figure 3c,d). We observed that the fraction of deep layer-restricted lineages labeled with MADM (~7%) is smaller than that obtained with retroviral tracing (15%)
evidence: This claim is supported by MADM experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: MADM experiments did not recover a significant number of superficial layer-restricted lineages.
source: In contrast, we did not recover a significant number of superficial layer-restricted lineages in MADM experiments (Figure 3d).
evidence: This claim is supported by MADM experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Approximately 75% of lineages labeled by injection of Emx1-CreERT2;RCL-Gfp mice with low tamoxifen doses at E12.5 were translaminar.
source: Consistent with the other approaches, the majority of lineages (~75%) labeled by injection of Emx1-CreERT2;RCL-Gfp mice with low tamoxifen doses at E12.5 were translaminar (Figure 4b,e).
evidence: This claim is supported by genetic fate mapping experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Approximately 13% of lineages in Emx1-CreERT2;RCL-Gfp experiments were restricted to deep cortical layers.
source: We also confirmed that ~13% of the lineages were restricted to deep cortical layers (Figure 4c,e).
evidence: This claim is supported by genetic fate mapping experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Approximately 11% of lineages in Emx1-CreERT2;RCL-Gfp experiments consist of pyramidal cells confined to superficial layers of the neocortex.
source: In addition, we found that ~11% of the lineages consist of PCs confined to superficial layers of the neocortex (Figure 4d,e and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by genetic fate mapping experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The combined results of three different lineage-tracing experiments suggest that translaminar (~80%), deep layer-restricted (~10%) and superficial layer-restricted (~10%) lineages are generated at the onset of neurogenesis in the developing neocortex.
source: In sum, the combined results of three different sets of lineage-tracing experiments suggested that translaminar (~80%), deep layer-restricted (~10%) and superficial layer-restricted (~10%) lineages are generated at the onset of neurogenesis in the developing neocortex.
evidence: This claim is a summary of data from multiple experimental approaches.

claim: Only about a quarter of traced lineages contains neurons in every cortical layer from II to VI.
source: In lineage-tracing experiments using Emx1-CreERT2;RCL-Gfp mice (Figure 5a), we observed that only about a quarter of traced lineages contains neurons in every cortical layer from II to VI, and every other clone lacks neurons in one or multiple cortical layers (Figure 5b–d,f).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Pyramidal cell lineages adopt every possible configuration of laminar distributions in the neocortex.
source: considered collectively, PC lineages adopt every possible configuration of laminar distributions in the neocortex (Figure 5f).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The clonal size of cortical lineages follows a bimodal distribution, with maximums at approximately four and eight cells.
source: Although the clonal size of these lineages also exhibits great heterogeneity, it seems to follow a bimodal distribution, with maximums at approximately four and eight cells (Figure 5e).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Translaminar lineages typically show a bias toward the production of pyramidal cells for superficial layers.
source: This analysis revealed that these cortical lineages typically showed a bias toward the production of PCs for superficial layers, although a minority of lineages displayed a preference toward deep layers or a balanced distribution across deep- and superficial layers (Figure 5g).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Nearly a quarter of all-layer translaminar lineages are composed exclusively by cortico-cortical projection neurons (CCPNs).
source: Using this classification, we found that nearly a quarter of all-layer translaminar lineages were composed exclusively by CCPNs, while multiple different combinations of PC identities comprise the remaining lineages (Figure 5h).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Only a minor fraction of all cortical lineages contains the entire complement of pyramidal cell subtypes.
source: Of note, only a minor fraction of all cortical lineages contains the entire complement of subtypes identified.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data on pyramidal cell subtype composition.

claim: There are no significant differences in the average clonal size or in the relative frequency of translaminar and laminar-restricted lineages between P2 and P21.
source: We detected no significant differences in the average clonal size or in the relative frequency of P2 translaminar and laminar-restricted lineages compared to P21 (Figure 5—figure supplement 3a–d).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing P2 and P21 lineages.

claim: The diversity of lineage patterns is remarkably similar between P2 and P21.
source: In addition, we observed that the diversity of lineage patterns was remarkably similar between P2 and P21 (Figure 5—figure supplement 3e).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing P2 and P21 lineages.

claim: The heterogeneity in cortical lineages arises directly during the process of cortical neurogenesis.
source: These experiments suggested that although cell death may have a subtle impact in refining the final diversity of lineages and their relative proportion, such heterogeneity should arise directly during the process of cortical neurogenesis.
evidence: This claim is inferred from experimental data comparing P2 and P21 lineages.

claim: The laminar distribution of neurons within each lineage arises specifically from an organized pattern of neurogenesis.
source: These results indicated that the laminar distribution of neurons within each lineage arises specifically from an organized pattern of neurogenesis.
evidence: This claim is inferred from permutation analysis results.

claim: Models using one or two progenitor types are sufficient to produce a diversity of lineage compositions as found in experimental data.
source: The Bayesian inference approach revealed that models using one or two progenitor types are sufficient to produce a diversity of lineage compositions as found in our experimental data (Figure 6a,e,f).
evidence: This claim is supported by Bayesian modeling results shown in Figure 6.

claim: A stochastic model based on a single, equipotent VZ progenitor cell was able to reproduce the majority of experimentally observed lineage features.
source: In agreement with the Bayesian approach, we found that a stochastic model based on a single, equipotent VZ progenitor cell (Model 1), that is a single set of cell generation probabilities, was able to reproduce the majority of experimentally observed lineage features.
evidence: This claim is supported by mathematical modeling results.

claim: Model 1 generated lineages with an exaggerated anti-correlation in the number of cells in superficial versus deep layers.
source: However, this model generated lineages with an exaggerated anti-correlation in the number of cells in superficial versus deep layers (Figure 7—figure supplement 1d)
evidence: This claim is supported by mathematical modeling results shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Model 1 failed to reproduce the bimodal distribution of clonal sizes.
source: and failed to reproduce the bimodal distribution of clonal sizes, underestimating the fraction of small lineages (those containing 3–4 cells).
evidence: This claim is supported by mathematical modeling results.

claim: Model 2 with two different progenitor populations faithfully reproduced all the experimental features in the data.
source: We found that this model faithfully reproduced all the experimental features in our data: total laminar fractions (Figure 7b), bimodal distribution of clonal sizes (Figure 7c) and negative correlation in superficial versus deep layers (Figure 7d).
evidence: This claim is supported by mathematical modeling results shown in Figure 7.

claim: Mathematical modeling suggests that a stochastic mechanism of cortical neurogenesis based on two independent progenitor cell populations best approximates the experimental data.
source: In sum, mathematical modeling suggests that a stochastic mechanism of cortical neurogenesis based on two independent progenitor cell populations best approximates the experimental data.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion from mathematical modeling results.

claim: Important differences in laminar cytoarchitecture exist between the primary somatosensory (S1) and visual (V1) cortices.
source: As expected, we found important differences in laminar cytoarchitecture between both regions (Figure 7g).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Subtle tuning of generation probabilities is sufficient to replicate different laminar ratios in silico for different cortical areas.
source: Remarkably, we found that subtle tuning of generation probabilities for both areas was sufficient to replicate the different laminar ratios in silico (Figure 7h).
evidence: This claim is supported by mathematical modeling results shown in Figure 7.

claim: The output of individual progenitor cells in the developing mouse neocortex is much more heterogeneous than previously anticipated.
source: Our results indicate that the output of individual progenitor cells in the developing mouse neocortex is much more heterogeneous than previously anticipated.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the experimental results.

claim: A sizable fraction of cortical lineages lacks pyramidal cells in one or several layers.
source: However, a sizable fraction of those lineages lacks PCs in one or several layers.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from lineage tracing experiments.

claim: The heterogeneous output of cortical progenitor cells includes lineages in which pyramidal cells are restricted to either deep or superficial layers.
source: In addition, the heterogeneous output of cortical progenitor cells includes lineages in which PCs are restricted to either deep or superficial layers.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from lineage tracing experiments.

claim: The wide diversity of progenitor outputs is compatible with a stochastic model of cortical neurogenesis.
source: Mathematical modeling suggests that this wide diversity of outputs is compatible with a stochastic model of cortical neurogenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by mathematical modeling results.

claim: The stochastic model represents a robust and adaptable mechanism for the assembly of neocortical cytoarchitecture.
source: Such model represents a robust and adaptable mechanism for the assembly of neocortical cytoarchitecture.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the modeling results.

claim: Retroviral labeling only labels hemi-lineages and is prone to silencing.
source: Retroviral labeling has two important limitations: it only labels hemi-lineages and is prone to silencing, which may prevent the identification of the entire progeny of a progenitor cell (Cepko et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim describes known limitations of retroviral labeling supported by a citation.

claim: Retroviral labeling targets progenitor cells indiscriminately and is not biased toward a particular genetic fate.
source: Conversely, retroviral labeling targets progenitor cells indiscriminately and, consequently, is not biased toward a particular genetic fate (Cepko et al., 2000), as is the case for genetic strategies.
evidence: This claim describes an advantage of retroviral labeling supported by a citation.

claim: MADM G2-X events require progenitor cells to undergo cell division at the time of induction.
source: However, G2-X MADM events require progenitor cells to undergo cell division at the time of induction because it directly relies on Cre-dependent inter-chromosomal mitotic recombination (Zong et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim describes a characteristic of MADM supported by a citation.

claim: MADM does not reliably label a small fraction of progenitor cells present in the pallial VZ at E12.5 that gives rise to cohorts of pyramidal cells exclusively located in superficial layers of the neocortex.
source: Our results revealed that MADM does not reliably label a small fraction of progenitor cells present in the pallial VZ at E12.5 that gives rise to cohorts of PCs exclusively located in superficial layers of the neocortex.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of experimental results from different methods.

claim: Some Emx1+ progenitor cells producing exclusively superficial layer pyramidal cells in the developing cortex are not targeted by the MADM approach.
source: These lineages were however observed in both retroviral labeling experiments and in genetic tracing experiments using the same genetic driver (Emx1-CreERT2) as in the MADM experiments, which strongly suggests that some Emx1+ progenitor cells producing exclusively superficial layer PCs in the developing cortex are not targeted by the MADM approach.
evidence: This claim is inferred from comparison of experimental results from different methods.

claim: Some progenitors producing superficial layer pyramidal cells might be quiescent or slow-dividing progenitors at E12.5 and become more active at later stages of development.
source: We hypothesize that these progenitors might be quiescent or slow-dividing progenitors at this stage and become more active at later stages of development.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed to explain the experimental observations.

claim: Genetic fate-mapping strategies cannot distinguish between symmetric proliferating and asymmetric neurogenic divisions.
source: Finally, although the use of genetic fate-mapping strategies (e.g. Emx1-CreERT2;RCL-Gfp) is a powerful method to investigate cortical lineages, it has the important constraint of not being able to distinguish between symmetric proliferating and asymmetric neurogenic divisions.
evidence: This claim describes a limitation of genetic fate-mapping strategies.

claim: Previous clonal analyses based on MADM failed to identify lineages with restricted laminar patterns.
source: Previous clonal analyses based on MADM lineage tracing experiments led to the suggestion that individual progenitor cells in the pallial VZ produce a unitary output of approximately eight excitatory neocortical neurons distributed throughout superficial and deep layers of the neocortex (Gao et al., 2014). However, those studies failed to identify lineages with restricted laminar patterns (either deep or superficial layer restricted clones).
evidence: This claim describes limitations of previous studies supported by a citation.

claim: Previous studies underestimated the fraction of lineages with relatively small clonal size.
source: Consequently, they also underestimated the fraction of lineages with relatively small clonal size.
evidence: This claim is inferred from comparison with previous studies.

claim: The analysis of neurogenic lineages revealed a bimodal distribution of clonal sizes with defined peaks centered at approximately four and eight cells.
source: In contrast, our analysis of neurogenic lineages revealed a bimodal distribution of clonal sizes with defined peaks centered at approximately four and eight cells, which largely correspond to the contribution of laminar-restricted and translaminar lineages, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from lineage tracing.

claim: Approximately one in six cortical progenitor cells generate laminar-restricted lineages.
source: In our experiments, approximately one in six cortical progenitor cells generate laminar-restricted lineages.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from lineage tracing.

claim: The existence of lineages restricted to deep layers of the neocortex was observed with all three methods used in this study.
source: The existence of lineages restricted to deep layers of the neocortex was observed with all three methods used in this study.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from multiple methods.

claim: Both retroviral labeling and genetic fate-mapping experiments identified a fraction of cortical progenitor cells that generate pyramidal cells that exclusively populate the superficial layers of the neocortex.
source: In addition, both retroviral labeling and genetic fate-mapping experiments identified a fraction of cortical progenitor cells that generate PCs that exclusively populate the superficial layers of the neocortex.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from two methods.

claim: The existence of superficial layer-restricted cortical lineages is supported by the identification of IPCs as early as E12.5 that generate superficial layer pyramidal cells.
source: The existence of superficial layer-restricted cortical lineages is further supported by the identification of IPCs as early as E12.5 that generate superficial layer PCs (this study and Mihalas et al., 2016), when the majority of deep layer PCs are being generated.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from this study and a citation.

claim: Some progenitors are tuned to generate superficial layer pyramidal cells from early stages of corticogenesis.
source: Since IPCs derive from VZ progenitor cells (Haubensak et al., 2004; Miyata et al., 2004; Noctor et al., 2004) and cortical neurogenesis begins at these stages in the mouse, this observation reinforces the idea that some progenitors are tuned to generate superficial layer PCs from early stages of corticogenesis.
evidence: This claim is inferred from experimental observations and supported by citations.

claim: Most translaminar lineages arise from progressive divisions of individual progenitor cells.
source: The results of those experiments indicate that symmetric divisions at E12.5 generate at least one translaminar sub-lineage in virtually all cases (58/59), suggesting that most translaminar lineages arise from progressive divisions of individual progenitor cells.
evidence: This claim is inferred from MADM experimental results.

claim: Most cortical progenitors generate diverse types of excitatory neurons.
source: Consistent with this idea, our results reveal that most cortical progenitors generate diverse types of excitatory neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data on pyramidal cell subtype composition.

claim: The majority of cortical lineages does not include the entire diversity of excitatory neurons.
source: However, since many cortical progenitor cells fail to generate neurons for at least one layer of the neocortex, the majority of cortical lineages does not include the entire diversity of excitatory neurons.
evidence: This claim is inferred from experimental data on lineage composition.

claim: The fraction of individual cortical lineages that contain all three main classes of excitatory projection neurons is significantly smaller than previously anticipated.
source: In other words, the fraction of individual cortical lineages that would be considered as 'canonical' – that is containing all three main classes of excitatory projection neurons (CCPN, SCPN and CThPN) – is significantly smaller than previously anticipated.
evidence: This claim is inferred from experimental data on lineage composition.

claim: Cortical progenitor cells exhibit very heterogeneous patterns of neuronal generation and specification.
source: Considering the variance in clonal size and lineage composition of neocortical lineages, our results indicate that cortical progenitor cells exhibit very heterogeneous patterns of neuronal generation and specification.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion from experimental data.

claim: The neuronal output of RGCs is not deterministic.
source: This interpretation challenges the view that the neuronal output of RGCs is deterministic (Gao et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is a conclusion that challenges a previous view supported by a citation.

claim: Stochastic developmental programs in which cortical progenitors undergo probability-based decisions are capable of generating the wide diversity of lineage configurations observed in experiments.
source: Our results indicate that stochastic developmental programs, in which cortical progenitors undergo a series of probability-based decisions for the generation of the different PC fates, are capable of generating the wide diversity of lineage configurations observed in our experiments.
evidence: This claim is supported by mathematical modeling results.

claim: The genesis of diverse neocortical lineages does not require a corresponding heterogeneity in VZ progenitors.
source: Therefore, in spite of the great diversity of configurations that exist among individual neocortical lineages, our results suggest that their genesis does not require a corresponding heterogeneity in VZ progenitors.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion from modeling results.

claim: The stochastic model proposed is reminiscent of that described for the developing rodent and zebrafish retina.
source: The model proposed here is somewhat reminiscent of that described for the developing rodent and zebrafish retina (Gomes et al., 2011; He et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim compares the proposed model to previous models supported by citations.

claim: Stochastic mechanisms based on a single set of probability rules explain the genesis of most, but not all neuronal types in the mammalian retina.
source: In line with our findings, stochastic mechanisms based on a single set of probability rules explain the genesis of most, but not all neuronal types in the mammalian retina (Gomes et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work on retinal development.

claim: Previous studies have identified morphological heterogeneity among pallial VZ progenitor cells.
source: Previous studies have identified morphological heterogeneity among pallial VZ progenitor cells (Gal et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: There is limited evidence for important molecular differences among VZ progenitor cells.
source: However, there is limited evidence for important molecular differences among these cells (Mizutani et al., 2007; Pollen et al., 2014; Telley et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: A homogeneous population of progenitor cells following a common developmental program explains most of the observed outcomes but fails to generate the fraction of small superficial lineages.
source: our results suggest that while a homogeneous population of progenitor cells following a common developmental program explains most of the observed outcomes, it fails to generate the fraction of small superficial lineages observed in the experiments.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion from mathematical modeling results.

claim: The introduction of a second population of progenitor cells is required to reproduce small superficial lineages.
source: The introduction of a second population of progenitor cells is required to reproduce these lineages.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion from mathematical modeling results.

claim: Progenitor cells in different cortical areas are likely constrained by different probabilistic rules.
source: Our study suggests that progenitor cells in different cortical areas are likely constrained by different probabilistic rules, which would contribute to the generation of the diverse cytoarchitectonic patterns found across the neocortex.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion from modeling results.

claim: Lineages located in different cortical areas exhibit features that reflect the local cytoarchitecture.
source: Although the number of lineages recovered from each cortical region is insufficient to provide conclusive evidence for major regional differences, lineages located in different cortical areas seem to exhibit features that reflect the local cytoarchitecture.
evidence: This claim is based on observations from experimental data.

claim: Lineages lacking layer IV neurons were abundantly found in the retrosplenial cingulate and motor cortices, where this layer is remarkably small.
source: For instance, lineages lacking layer IV neurons were abundantly found in the retrosplenial cingulate and motor cortices, where this layer is remarkably small.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations.

claim: Stochastic neurogenic decisions likely depend on the influence of extrinsic and intrinsic signals on parameters such as cell cycle length, asymmetric inheritance of cell components, generation of dividing versus postmitotic progeny, and membrane potential of progenitor cells.
source: How and when stochastic neurogenic decisions are made remains to be elucidated, but they likely depend on the influence of extrinsic and intrinsic signals on parameters such as cell cycle length, the asymmetric inheritance of cell components, the generation of dividing (IPCs) versus postmitotic progeny, and the membrane potential of progenitor cells (Haydar et al., 2003; Lange et al., 2009; Pilaz et al., 2009; Roccio et al., 2013; Vitali et al., 2018; Wang et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is speculative and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Local signals in different neocortical areas would contribute to the tuning of progenitor cell behaviors to output different cytoarchitectures without the requirement of regional-specific progenitor populations.
source: Local signals in different neocortical areas would contribute to the tuning of progenitor cell behaviors to output different cytoarchitectures without the requirement of regional-specific progenitor populations.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion from the modeling results.

claim: The stochastic model allows great flexibility in the generation of heterogeneous cortical cytoarchitectures without the requirement of a large number of progenitor identities.
source: Consequently, this model allows great flexibility in the generation of heterogeneous cortical cytoarchitectures without the requirement of a large number of progenitor identities.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the modeling results.

claim: The specification of a very small number of progenitor cells with competence to adapt their neurogenic behavior to different probabilistic rules represents the most parsimonious and robust mechanism for the generation of cortical circuitry.
source: The specification of a very small number of progenitor cells with competence to adapt their neurogenic behavior to different probabilistic rules based on their location within the neocortical neuroepithelium represents the most parsimonious and robust mechanism for the generation of cortical circuitry.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the modeling results.
